wk2_unpaid_ot.text: Your supervisor strolls over at 4:55. 'We need you this weekend. No extra pay, but it shows commitment.'

outcomes.respected: He grunts, nods, and finds someone else. You get a little more respect.
outcomes.noted: He writes something down. You are now 'not a team player'.
outcomes.cathartic: The whole floor heard. You are a legend for about a day.
outcomes.fired: Security arrives before you finish your sentence. Your badge stops working.
outcomes.warning: A formal warning lands in your file.

wk2_ot_crunch.text: A launch is slipping. The team is sleeping at the office. Pizza boxes cover every flat surface.

outcomes.smooth: You split the work smartly. It ships on time, and nobody cries.
outcomes.mess: The plan collapses at 3 a.m. You end up doing it all anyway.

wk2_gossip_war.text: Two coworkers are feuding and both want you on their side. Lunch has become a diplomatic summit.

outcomes.peace: They shake hands, grudgingly. You're the office diplomat now.
outcomes.both_hate: They unite against you. Impressive, really.

wk2_desk_thief.text: Your good stapler, your good mug, and your good chair have all vanished. Someone is shopping from your desk.

outcomes.caught: You catch a coworker red-handed. Awkward, but you get the chair back.
outcomes.wrong: You accuse the wrong person. The apology cake is on you.

wk2_office_crush.text: A colleague has been lingering by your desk. You both pretend it's about spreadsheets. It is not about spreadsheets.

outcomes.yes: They say yes. You spend the week smiling at nothing.
outcomes.no: A polite no. Now every coffee run is a hostage negotiation.

wk2_crush_married.text: After the team dinner, a married coworker walks you to your car and doesn't walk away.

outcomes.secret: One night. Then a secret that follows you into every meeting.
outcomes.exposed: Someone saw. By Monday the whole office knows.

wk2_crush_aftermath.text: The fling with your coworker ended badly. You still share a printer, a kitchen, and a Tuesday meeting.

wk2_hr_complaint.text: HR calls you in. A coworker filed a complaint about a joke you made. You remember the joke. It was not good.

outcomes.cleared: HR decides it's a misunderstanding. A mandatory training slide deck is your only punishment.
outcomes.written: A written warning, and a very long video about respect.

wk2_hr_false.text: A coworker accuses you of something you didn't do. Their story has details that almost fit.

outcomes.vindicated: Your records clear you in minutes. The accuser is reassigned.
outcomes.shrug: Inconclusive. The cloud hangs over you for months.

wk2_report_harass.text: You watch a manager corner a junior coworker at the party. She looks at you across the room, asking silently.

outcomes.justice: He's quietly gone within a month. She thanks you at the coffee machine.
outcomes.retaliation: He stays. Your next review is mysteriously harsh.

wk2_report_thief.text: You see a coworker pocketing company supplies. Then a laptop. Then, slowly, the whole supply closet.

outcomes.stops: They go red, return the stuff, and avoid you for a month.
outcomes.threat: They deny it, and now they have a grudge.

wk2_union_drive.text: Someone slid a union flyer under your keyboard. Management sent an email about 'a family culture' the same afternoon.

outcomes.win: The vote passes. Pay and hours improve for everyone.
outcomes.crushed: Management fights it. Your name ends up on a list.

wk2_union_strike.text: The union calls a one-day strike. The picket line is cold, loud, and surprisingly well-catered.

wk2_layoff_rumor.text: Everyone is whispering. The big boss is flying in. Three people have already updated their resumes.

outcomes.safe: Your name stays off the list. The empty desk next to you is not yours.
outcomes.cut: Cut anyway. A box, a hug, a handshake.
outcomes.rattled: Nothing happens. You age five years in the waiting.

wk2_layoff_survivor.text: Layoffs happened. You survived. The team shrank by a third and the workload did not.

outcomes.laughed: They remind you that you are lucky to have a job.

wk2_perf_review.text: Annual review day. Your manager has a printed form, a nervous smile, and a speech about 'trajectory'.

outcomes.great: Strong review. A decent raise lands next payroll.
outcomes.ok: 'Meets expectations.' The most beige phrase ever invented.
outcomes.bad: He lists every mistake since the last review.

wk2_client_free.text: A big client wants 'just a small thing' done for free. It would take you a week. He mentions future contracts.

outcomes.pays: He grumbles and pays. Respect, of a sort.
outcomes.walks: He leaves in a huff and your boss isn't happy.

wk2_client_late.text: A client is ninety days late on a big invoice and answers your emails with emojis only.

outcomes.paid: The money arrives within two days.
outcomes.lost: He's furious. The account quietly goes elsewhere.

wk2_credit_theft.text: Your boss presents your idea to the executives as his own. You are standing right there holding the slide clicker.

outcomes.noticed: The execs turn and look at you. Suddenly you have a future.
outcomes.punished: He smiles through his teeth. He'll remember this.

wk2_idea_meeting.text: In a meeting, a coworker repeats your point with more confidence and gets the applause.

wk2_retreat.text: The company sends everyone to a retreat in the countryside. There will be trust falls and a ropes course and a very enthusiastic facilitator.

outcomes.noticed: A director remembers your name. Voluntarily.
outcomes.cringe: You overshoot. 'Desperate' is the word going around.

wk2_retreat_fall.text: At the retreat, you're asked to fall backwards into your teammates' arms. Their expressions say 'maybe'.

outcomes.caught: They catch you. Somehow it works. You nearly tear up.
outcomes.dropped: The ground catches you instead. Everyone is very sorry.

wk2_work_injury.text: A shelf, a ladder, a wet floor. Something goes wrong and you are suddenly on your back looking at the ceiling tiles.

outcomes.minor: A sprain and a week of rest. Workers' comp covers most of it.
outcomes.serious: Broken bone. Months of physio and a lot of paperwork.
outcomes.fatal: It was worse than it looked. The ambulance came too late.
outcomes.settle: They settle quietly. You get paid, and you get stared at.

wk2_rsi.text: Your wrist has started to hum with a low, expensive pain. The doctor says 'ergonomics' like it's a diagnosis.

wk2_embezzle_temptation.text: A calculation error in the books leaves $30,000 in an account nobody checks. You are the only one who knows.

outcomes.clean: No one ever looks. You buy things and sleep badly.
outcomes.caught: The audit finds it. The police call that afternoon.

wk2_petty_cash.text: The petty cash drawer is unlocked. It has $200. Rent is due on Friday.

outcomes.repay: You put it back before payday. Your heart is still pounding.
outcomes.seen: A camera behind the plant saw everything.

wk2_referral_friend.text: A friend whispers: their company is hiring for a better role. Higher pay, nicer office, real title. They can vouch for you.

outcomes.in: You interview well. The offer comes fast.
outcomes.out: They went with someone cheaper. Your friend says sorry.
outcomes.counter: Your boss counters with a raise.
outcomes.bluff: He calls your bluff. Now it's awkward.

wk2_referral_give.text: A friend asks you to put in a good word for them at your company. They are charming. They are also late to everything.

outcomes.embarrass: They are late on day one. And day two.

wk2_headhunter.text: A headhunter slides into your inbox with 'an exciting opportunity'. The email has no salary and eleven exclamation marks.

wk2_lie_customer.text: A customer asks if the product will arrive by Friday. It will not. Your manager nods at you to say yes.

outcomes.luck: It arrives Friday by a miracle.
outcomes.blowup: It does not. The customer is not nice about it.

wk2_backdate_doc.text: Your boss asks you to backdate a contract so an audit will pass. 'Everyone does it.'

outcomes.fine: Nothing happens. The knot in your stomach stays.
outcomes.audit: The auditor circles the date twice.

wk2_four_day_week.text: The company launches a four-day work week pilot. Management insists productivity must stay the same. Fridays are suddenly yours.

choices.sidegig: Use it for a side gig

outcomes.pace: You find a rhythm. The pilot becomes permanent.
outcomes.burn: You work the same hours with less sleep.

wk2_remote_work.text: Your team goes remote for the season. Your bed is now two metres from your desk. So is your fridge.

outcomes.nobody: Nobody notices. You count the extra money.
outcomes.busted: A coworker sees both of your names on the same call.

wk2_printer_war.text: The office printer is jammed again. Notes appear on it: 'Fix it', 'Who broke it', 'I KNOW who broke it'.

outcomes.hero: You pull out a crumpled sandwich wrapper. You are a hero.
outcomes.worse: It starts smoking. The fire alarm answers.

wk2_holiday_disaster.text: The holiday party has an open bar. By 10 p.m., Gary from accounting is on the table and the CEO is crying.

outcomes.legend: You dance like nobody is watching. Everybody is watching. It's a hit.
outcomes.shame: You tell the CEO what you really think. He remembers every word.

wk2_holiday_bonus.text: Bonus season. The envelope is thinner than last year's. Someone in marketing got a boat.

outcomes.none: They give you a lecture about 'being a team'.

wk2_burnout.text: You stare at your screen and feel nothing. The emails are blurred. The thought of tomorrow is a wall.

outcomes.ok: You limp along. Nothing breaks. Yet.
outcomes.crash: You break in the shower on a Wednesday. It's a long fall.

wk2_burnout_vacation.text: You haven't had a day off in eleven months. Your manager says 'whenever works' with a look that means 'never'.

choices.sick: Call in sick for a week

outcomes.rested: A week of nothing. It's glorious.
outcomes.suspicious: HR asks for a doctor's note. You don't have one.

wk2_retirement_party.text: They throw you a retirement party. There's a sheet cake with your name misspelled and a card signed by people who don't know you.

outcomes.tears: The room gets very quiet. A few people wipe their eyes.
outcomes.rambled: You ramble for twenty minutes. People clap out of mercy.

wk2_retirement_push.text: The company offers you early retirement with a modest package. Your boss says 'it's time for fresh blood'.

outcomes.stays: They back off. You keep your desk, and your enemies.
outcomes.pushed: They find a reason soon after. You leave with less.

wk2_whistleblow_big.text: You find proof that the company is dumping waste illegally. You have the files on a USB stick. Your hand shakes.

outcomes.payout: The investigation wins. A regulator rewards you with a major payout.
outcomes.crushed: The company buries you. You become 'the one who talked'.

wk2_promotion_board.text: A seat opened up. The promotion board has three people in dark suits and a clipboard. They ask: 'Where do you see yourself in five years?'

outcomes.promoted: Two weeks later: a new title, a new desk, a new type of stress.
outcomes.passed_over: They picked someone with better hair. You aren't bitter.
outcomes.liked: They laugh, and the joke lands you the job.

wk2_promotion_denied.text: You didn't get the promotion. Your manager says 'next year', with the voice of someone who has said it before.

outcomes.real: Useful, honest notes. You write them down.

wk2_new_boss.text: A new manager arrives. She rearranges the seating chart, bans meetings on Fridays and learns everyone's coffee order. Suspicious.

outcomes.ally: She backs you in a tough meeting. Valuable.
outcomes.tool: People say you're the new boss's pet.

wk2_parking_war.text: Someone keeps parking in your spot. There are no names on the spots. Everyone knows whose it is.

outcomes.win: The car vanishes by lunch. You enjoy your spot.
outcomes.war: They key your door. This is now a war.

wk2_mandatory_fun.text: Mandatory fun day: karaoke at noon. Attendance is voluntary but also tracked.

outcomes.star: You nail the chorus. They ask for an encore.
outcomes.flat: The notes are not friends with your voice.

wk2_mentee.text: A fresh hire asks you to be their mentor. They remind you of yourself at their age, except better dressed.

outcomes.flourish: They flourish. You feel useful, and old.
outcomes.stuck: They are needy. You spend your afternoons holding hands.

wk2_merger.text: Rumours of a merger. The brochures say 'synergy'. The employees say 'layoffs with extra steps'.

outcomes.rise: The new company needs people who know the old systems. You.
outcomes.lost: You become a duplicate. The new company already has you.

wk2_ai_tool.text: The company rolls out a tool that does half your job in four minutes. Management calls it 'empowering'.

outcomes.replaced: You trained your replacement. Who thanks you with a muffin.

wk2_caught_sleeping.text: You nod off at your desk after lunch. When you wake, a manager is standing there holding a very large coffee.

choices.nap_home: Nap at home from now on

outcomes.buys: 'Deep work,' he says, and walks away impressed.
outcomes.no: He gave you a look. A look you will feel for weeks.

wk2_boss_affair.text: You walk into a supply closet and find your boss with someone who is definitely not their spouse.

outcomes.paid: You get a raise. And a lifelong nightmare.

wk2_coworker_collapse.text: A coworker collapses in the hallway. The room freezes. Someone shouts for someone to call an ambulance.

outcomes.saved: You keep them alive until the medics come. They send you flowers.
outcomes.too_late: They don't make it. Months later you still hear the compressions.

wk2_hire_interview.text: You're asked to interview a candidate. They are overqualified, nervous, and wearing a suit two sizes too small.

outcomes.great: Best hire of the year. They owe you a coffee.
outcomes.flop: They're gone in a month. The blame lands on you.

wk2_salary_leak.text: A spreadsheet with everyone's salary goes around by accident. You open it. You wish you hadn't.

outcomes.corrected: HR 'discovers a discrepancy'. Your pay jumps.
outcomes.punished: They say you have 'poor discretion'. Nothing changes.

wk2_lunch_drinks.text: A client lunch turns into a second bottle. Your boss orders a third. Everyone is loosening ties.

outcomes.bonded: The client is yours. The hangover is also yours.
outcomes.disaster: You tell the client a trade secret. Then cry.

wk2_rival_sabotage.text: A rival coworker 'accidentally' forwarded your draft to the whole department with the typos highlighted.

outcomes.even: You win the round. Both of you look petty.
outcomes.fail: Your plan leaks. Now you're the villain.

wk2_fire_someone.text: You've been told to let a good person go. The paperwork is on your desk. The call is in an hour.

choices.help: Help them find a new job

outcomes.spared: Management backs down. The person stays.
outcomes.both: You get fired too. At least you're consistent.

wk2_conference_trip.text: A conference abroad. Name tags, keynote speeches and an open bar in the hotel lobby with an interesting stranger.

outcomes.fun: A night to remember. Don't leave anything behind.
outcomes.caught: Someone posts a photo. It finds you before your flight.

wk2_holiday_shift.text: Your boss offers a flat bonus of $200 for working through the holiday. The holiday is your child's birthday.

outcomes.works: A coworker owes you. You owe them a favour.
outcomes.none: Nobody bites. You end up working anyway.

wk2_team_lead.text: Your boss offers you a team lead role: more responsibility, a small raise and a mug that says 'Okayest Boss'.

outcomes.shine: You thrive in the role. Your team is loyal.
outcomes.overwhelmed: Meetings, reports, emotional labour. You miss being a regular worker.

wk2_startup_pitch.text: A friend asks you to join a startup. It could be huge. It could be nothing. It would require quitting this job.

outcomes.boom: The startup pops. You cash out.
outcomes.bust: It fails. You're out of both jobs.

wk2_deadline_miss.text: You are about to miss a critical deadline. Your phone is lit with messages. Your heart is doing something rhythmic and wrong.

outcomes.made: You make it by five minutes.
outcomes.late: You deliver it at 8:01. It doesn't count.

wk2_nepotism_boss.text: The owner's nephew is hired above you. He does not know how to use the printer, and nobody who does is willing to tell him.

outcomes.ally: He learns quickly and becomes a useful ally.
outcomes.worse: He takes credit and thinks he's doing great.

wk2_quiet_quitting.text: You've hit the point where you do exactly what you're paid for and not a minute more. It feels weirdly peaceful.

outcomes.shift: He gives you a different project. It helps.

wk2_expense_padding.text: Your manager is padding expense reports. You know because you compiled them.

outcomes.praised: The company thanks you with a certificate and some distance.
outcomes.retaliated: He finds a new reason to dislike you every week.
